newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodian PM rejects threat to halt polls.
newsitem.headline: Cambodian PM rejects threat to halt polls.

text.p: Cambodian co-Premier Prince Norodom Ranariddh on Monday countered threats by his political rival to halt elections if the king abdicates, saying only parliament could postpone polls under the constitution.

"No one has the right to decide about having or not having the elections because according to our constitution only a two-thirds majority of the national assembly has the right to postpone the elections," the prince told reporters at the cabinet building.

Co-Premier Hun Sen, whose Cambodian People's Party (CPP) formed an uneasy alliance with the prince's royalist FUNCINPEC party after U.N.-run general elections in 1993, last week warned of a political crisis if King Norodom Sihanouk follows through on hints that he might abdicate.
Hun Sen said local and general elections due in 1997 and 1998 would have to be cancelled if the king left the throne and added that members of the royal family should be barred from politics.
Some analysts believe Hun Sen and his party fear the king might step down to lead a royalist party to victory at the polls on the back of his grassroots popularity.
Ranariddh reiterated that he did not want Sihanouk to abdicate as it would cause political instability.
But he added that if his 74-year-old father insisted on leaving the throne and entering politics, the royalists would have no choice but to support him.
He said leaders of the two parties were to meet later on Monday to discuss the latest issue in relations.

Sihanouk said last month he had been thinking of abdicating following mounting verbal attacks on himself and the royal family. But the monarch, who is only a figurehead, pledged never to take part in elections.

Relations between the CPP and FUNCINPEC deteriorated after Ranariddh demanded a fairer share of power in the coalition last year and worsened in recent months as the rivals vied for the support of thousands of Khmer Rouge guerrilla defectors.
The two men in recent weeks have formed rival alliances with other parties in preparation for the elections.
